Support for SockJS 1.0+; remove old SockJS support.
description:
The SockJS option protocol_whitelist was only valid with pre-1.0 releases.
Newer releases use the transports option.

The protocol chooser is updated to support "eventsource" and "htmlfile".

The option transportDebugging is no longer supported.

title: Adds travis jobs on ppc64le
description: This PR adds power support on travis.

title: Stop interfering with Bootstrap 4 tabs
description:
Our <base href> fixup logic modifies hrefs; basically we convert them to absolute URLs in order to prevent <base> from interfering. But this act of converting to absolute URLs messes up links that aren't for page navigation, but for interactive use--in particular, Bootstrap 4 tabs.

This PR identifies the latter case for Bootstrap 4, by not fixing up anchors with `data-toggle` attributes.

Fixes #17

title: Upgrade dependencies, especially to babel 7
description:
The code changes in this PR were required to pass updated eslint rules.

Note that none of the security-flagged packages were runtime dependencies, only devDependencies (required for transpiling, linting, and/or testing). Also note that merging this PR doesn't immediately affect Shiny Server or Connect, since they have to then upgrade the shiny-server-client commit they point to.

title: Un-whitelist the xhr-streaming transport on MS Edge instead of removing it as an option
description:
Recent changes removed `xhr-streaming` from the protocol chooser. This disables it by default instead. This will help give us a way to test `xhr-streaming` when Edge fixes whatever the underlying issue is.

It's possibly related to this, but there are some key differences in this bug report. Nevertheless, it seems to be linked to JS not receiving the streamed data outside of a polling interval: https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/platform/issues/12224510/

title: Triggered reconnect on 3000 WebSocket error
description:
When connection is lost and resumed, the client can receive a c[3000,"No response from heartbeat"] message. This causes the client to disconnect. This commit treats the 3000 error as a recoverable error, and try to reconnect.

This issue is triggered in Google Chrome, which doesn't send pings to check if connection is healthy. Safari and Firefox notice a dropped connection before this situation occurs.

title: send a dummy protocol instead of an empty whitelist
description:
SockJS regards an empty `protocols_whitelist` option as an indication that all
protocols should be enabled. To avoid this behavior, pass a "dummy" protocol to
SockJS when we end up with an empty set of whitelisted protocols. This isn't
useful in the real world but helps validate behavior when all protocols end up
disabled through whatever technique.

For a bit more context, `protocols_whitelist` is interpreted not as an empty set of protocols but as an unspecified whitelist, causing SockJS to revert to attempting all protocols here:
https://github.com/sockjs/sockjs-client/blob/v0.3.4/lib/sockjs.js#L23-L26

This is eventually interpreted at:
https://github.com/sockjs/sockjs-client/blob/v0.3.4/lib/utils.js#L280

Note that this PR also changes how the protocol chooser is exposed to lib/sockjs.js to make it easier to stub in test.
